description: The single versioned authority for which urn:agentbox kinds cross the agentbox -> VisionClaw federation boundary. Both translators derive their closed kind map from this file: the JS bridge (agentbox management-api/lib/bc20-provenance-bridge.js) reads it at load, and the Rust translator (VisionClaw src/uri/mod.rs::cross_from_agentbox) embeds it with include_str!("../../agentbox/schema/federation-kinds.json") - the agentbox tree is the ./agentbox submodule of the VisionClaw checkout, so that relative path resolves from src/uri/. Neither side may transcribe the kind list; a paired fixture asserts symmetry and any disagreement is a test failure.

conventions.content_address: sha256-12-<12 lowercase hex chars> = first 12 hex of sha256(payload)
conventions.hot_path: A crossing is evaluated with no side information beyond the URN itself. A kind that could only cross given extra arguments is crosses=false with an elevation block.

crossing_forms.identity: The owner pubkey IS the target identifier; structural round-trip, no content address.
crossing_forms.content-address-of-urn: The target local is sha256-12 of the whole source URN string; the source is recovered from a durable UrnMapping store.
crossing_forms.structural-passthrough: Source and target grammars are identical, so the existing content address is preserved rather than re-hashed; round-trips without a store.

refusal_classes.deliberate: A federated concept exists but the hot path cannot mint it without side information. Recorded, not absent - the crossing is deferred, never mis-mapped.
refusal_classes.not-federated: The kind has no VisionClaw counterpart at all. It is agentbox-local by design.

identity_passthrough.note: Already-converged identity. Both translators pass it through unchanged and reject a non-64-hex tail.

kinds.note: There is deliberately no urn:visionclaw:agent kind - an agent's identity IS its DID, so the crossing drops the human-readable name (node metadata, not identity).
The target is unscoped: the owner travels in owner_did and the UrnMapping, not in the identifier.
thing scope is optional in uris.js but required to cross - an unscoped thing has no owner to bind the personal KG node to.

Both grammars are <pubkey>:<sha256-12> since uris.js made bead contentAddressed (audit 2026-06-09 A3), so content identity is preserved across the boundary and the crossing needs no UrnMapping store. ADR-2061 resolved the direction in favour of crossing.

kinds.refusal_reason: memory -> concept needs the {domain, slug} elevation target, which the ingest hot path does not carry. Mapping it without those would fabricate a shared-ontology class from a private lesson, so the crossing is recorded raw and deferred to the governed elevation path.

elevation.rust_entry_point: uri::concept(domain, slug) - called by the governed elevation path, never by cross_from_agentbox
elevation.note: This is what makes the refusal distinguishable from 'not implemented': the target kind and the arguments that would unlock it are both recorded.

kinds.refusal_reason: Solid pod container in the agentbox sovereign data stack. VisionClaw has no pod surface; pod contents federate as their own typed kinds, never as the container.
Encrypted pod envelope. Crossing it would move ciphertext across a trust boundary that has no key material; the decrypted payload federates as its own kind instead.
Verifiable credential held in the agentbox identity layer. Authority is asserted by presentation to a verifier, not by federating the credential identifier.
Delegation mandate in the agentbox authority chain. Authority is evaluated agentbox-side before any crossing happens, so the mandate itself never leaves.
Payment/settlement receipt in the agentbox economy loop. VisionClaw has no settlement surface to bind it to.
Hash-chained agent event on the agentbox audit surface. Its chain position is only meaningful inside that chain, so only the derived activity crosses as an execution.

decision IS-A prov:Activity (ADR-048) but is governance-local: it records an agentbox authority act, not a VisionClaw execution. Federating it would let a governance record masquerade as compute provenance.
Owner-scoped dataset handle on the agentbox memory surface. VisionClaw has no dataset kind; dataset members federate individually where they federate at all.
MCP server registry entry - agentbox runtime tooling. It names a local process, which is meaningless outside this container.
Baked skill in the agentbox image. Image-local content addressed by name, with no VisionClaw counterpart.
Governance document identifier. Each repository owns its own ADR ledger; a cross-repo ADR reference is cited by URL, never minted as a foreign URN.
Governance document identifier - same reasoning as adr.
Governance document identifier - same reasoning as adr.
Reserved self-describing namespace for the URI scheme itself. Federating it would let the grammar describe a grammar it does not own.
